title: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming: Who Said What, While They're Still Saying It
hook: Unified speech-recognition-plus-diarization models beat running the two separately — but only offline. This one emits speaker-attributed transcripts as the audio arrives.
key_points: Traditional systems treat ASR and speaker diarization as separate stages; unified end-to-end models merged them but stayed offline.
Offline-only is a dealbreaker for real-time voice assistants and agents, which need low latency.
The approach interleaves fixed-size audio chunks, a small amount of lookahead audio, and previously emitted text.
That produces 'who said what' incrementally, with no separate diarization stage.
The 7B model reports the lowest average WER/CER across five evaluation sets and best-or-tied-best speaker attribution on 12 of 13 settings.
1.5B and 7B weights plus inference code are released.
content_html: Getting a transcript is one problem; knowing who spoke each line is another. Systems traditionally solved them separately — a recognizer plus a diarizer — until end-to-end models like VibeVoice-ASR folded both into one network. The catch was that those unified models ran offline, over complete recordings, which rules out real-time voice assistants and agents.
extra_html:
How it works

Tu and colleagues at Microsoft Research present what they describe as one of the first LLM-based end-to-end approaches to streaming speaker-attributed ASR. The input is interleaved: fixed-size audio chunks, a small amount of lookahead audio, and the text already produced. That structure lets the model emit "who said what" as speech arrives, still with no separate diarization stage.

Why it matters

The authors report their 7B model achieving the lowest average WER/CER across five evaluation sets, and the best or tied-best speaker attribution on 12 of 13 evaluation settings — so the streaming constraint doesn't obviously cost accuracy here. They release 1.5B and 7B weights together with inference code, which makes this directly usable rather than just a result to read about.

related.title: Whisper: Robust Speech Recognition at Scale
related.hook: Train a plain encoder-decoder transformer on 680,000 hours of weakly-labeled multilingual audio and you get near-human transcription robustness without task-specific fine-tuning.

related.title: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe
related.hook: Google DeepMind ships a speech-to-text model built on Gemini — pitching transcription that understands what it is hearing, not just what sounds were made.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'speaker-attributed ASR' add over plain speech recognition?
flashcards.back_html: It answers not just what was said but who said it — traditionally done by a separate diarization stage bolted onto the transcriber.

flashcards.prompt: How does VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming turn an offline unified model into a streaming one?

choices.text: It interleaves fixed-size audio chunks, a little lookahead audio, and previously emitted text
It runs the offline model repeatedly on a growing prefix of the audio
It adds a separate lightweight diarization model in front of the transcriber

flashcards.explanation_html: Chunked audio plus a small lookahead window plus prior text lets the model emit transcript and speaker labels incrementally, still without a separate diarization stage.
